plain_words: A full small milk tin of rice is about 175 g. About 6 tins make 1 kg. Your tin may be smaller or bigger, so check it once.
note: Sources disagree. The survey label says 175 g; figures in circulation run from about 100 g to about 200 g. At 175 g it is 6 tins per kg; at 100 g it would be 10.

plain_words: Some people use the bigger milk tin. No reliable weight found yet, so weigh yours.
note: The Guardian piece mentions both a 170 g and a 410 g tin.

plain_words: A small derica of rice is about 350 g. About 3 make 1 kg.
note: Surveys code small and big dericas separately (0.35 and 0.7 kg).

plain_words: A big derica of rice is about ¾ kg (700 to 780 g). A 50 kg bag holds about 64 to 71 big dericas.
note: Survey 0.7 kg; the Guardian says half a kongo (0.75 to 0.85 kg); the common rule of 64 dericas to a 50 kg bag gives 780 g.

plain_words: A kongo or mudu of rice is about 1½ kg, about 2 big dericas. Some mudus are smaller (nearer 1.1 kg), so check yours.
note: The survey lumps congo and mudu at 1.5 kg; the Guardian gives kongo as 1.5 to 1.7 kg; some mudus are smaller, near 1.1 kg. Later surveys code small, medium and large.

plain_words: A tiya is about 3 kg, about 2 kongos or mudus. Sizes differ where it is used, so ask.
note: No range found.

plain_words: A full 4-litre tin of rice is about 3 kg.
note: Guardian: about 2.75 kg. Four big dericas would give about 3.1 kg. Names clash: the Guardian calls the 4 L tin a 'painter', while elsewhere that name goes to the 20 L bucket. Ask the seller how many litres.

plain_words: A big 20-litre paint bucket of rice is about 12½ kg (a quarter of a 50 kg bag) if it is not filled to the very top. Filled to the brim it could be near 16 kg.
note: A quarter of a 50 kg bag is 12.5 kg (rule of thumb). Filled to the brim, 20 litres of rice would be near 16 kg.

group: Water test (compared with the same amount of water)
plain_words: Rice weighs about ⅘ as much as the same amount of water. Example: a tin that holds 200 g of water holds about 160 g of rice.
note: Nigerian rice varieties measured 0.59 to 0.90; 0.75 to 0.85 is the typical middle.

group: Water test (compared with the same amount of water)
plain_words: Beans (cowpea) weighs about ⅔ to ¾ as much as the same amount of water. Example: a tin that holds 200 g of water holds about 145 g of beans (cowpea).
note: Ghana cowpea variety; moisture changes it.

group: Water test (compared with the same amount of water)
plain_words: Garri weighs about ⅗ as much as the same amount of water. Example: a tin that holds 200 g of water holds about 125 g of garri.
note: West African garri samples.

group: Water test (compared with the same amount of water)
plain_words: Bambara nut weighs about ¾ as much as the same amount of water. Example: a tin that holds 200 g of water holds about 150 g of bambara nut.

group: Water test (compared with the same amount of water)
plain_words: Groundnut in the shell weighs about ¼ as much as the same amount of water. Example: a tin that holds 200 g of water holds about 55 g of groundnut in the shell.
note: Pods of three Nigerian varieties.

group: Water test (compared with the same amount of water)
plain_words: Egusi seeds in the shell weighs about ⅖ as much as the same amount of water. Example: a tin that holds 200 g of water holds about 80 g of egusi seeds in the shell.

plain_words: Cooked rice weighs about 2½ to 3 times as much as dry rice.

plain_words: Cooked beans weigh about 3 times as much as dry beans.
